name: FERC Pipeline Certificate Review
description: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for interstate natural gas pipelines.
key_delay_factors: NEPA EIS preparation; CWA Section 401 state certification; ESA Section 7 consultation; landowner opposition; GHG emissions analysis
quantitative_impact: No statutory time limit; ~95% approval rate historically; 20% of projects delayed 90+ days beyond FERC deadline
recent_changes: DC Circuit vacated Transco REAE pipeline (July 2024) for inadequate GHG analysis; increased uncertainty
reform_status: Certificate Policy Statement under review since 2022

name: LNG Terminal FERC Authorization
description: FERC authorization for siting, construction, and operation of onshore LNG export terminals.
key_delay_factors: Full EIS required; environmental justice review; GHG emissions analysis; state and local permits; community opposition
quantitative_impact: Average 158 days from EIS to approval (2015-2022); 20 FERC approvals totaling 27.2 Bcf/d capacity
affected_project_types: LNG export terminals, LNG import terminals
recent_changes: Trump administration 2025 expedited procedures; FERC considering blanket authorization for routine modifications
reform_status: November 2025 NOI on streamlining LNG approvals

name: DOE LNG Export Authorization
description: DOE authorization for LNG exports. FTA countries automatic. Non-FTA requires public interest determination.
key_delay_factors: Biden LNG pause (Jan 2024); economic/environmental review methodology under revision; litigation
quantitative_impact: ~50 Bcf/d approved capacity; 14.28 Bcf/d operating; ~10 Bcf/d affected by pause
recent_changes: Biden LNG pause on non-FTA authorizations (Jan 2024); 7-year export commencement deadline policy (2023)
reform_status: Pause in effect; Trump administration expected to lift pause

name: PJM Generator Interconnection Queue
description: PJM interconnection study process for new generation. Currently taking 6-8 years for projects entering 2018-2020.
key_delay_factors: Queue backlog from 2018-2020 projects; network upgrade costs ($240/kW average); restudy triggers; speculative projects
quantitative_impact: ~140 GW processed 2023-2024; 46 GW with signed agreements; 63 GW remaining; capacity prices jumped 10x due to queue delays
affected_project_types: Solar, wind, battery storage, natural gas generation
recent_changes: PJM Transition Cycle 1 completed Sept 2024; 1-2 year study turnaround expected for new projects post-2026
reform_status: FERC Order 2023 implemented; first-ready, first-served model

name: MISO Generator Interconnection Queue
description: MISO Definitive Planning Phase interconnection study process. Projects from 2018-2019 still in queue.
key_delay_factors: 242 GW in queue; 2023 queue window closed; 650-day average delays; 25 GW approved resources experiencing delays
quantitative_impact: 283 projects from 2022 cycle in Central region still awaiting study; 369 projects in South region
recent_changes: 2024 queue window delayed; 2023 projects expected to reach GIA execution by 2026
reform_status: Queue reforms implemented; backlog clearing expected by 2026

name: CAISO Generator Interconnection Queue
description: CAISO cluster study process for generator interconnection.
key_delay_factors: High queue volume; limited transmission capacity; restudy requirements
quantitative_impact: Only ~19% of projects nationally complete interconnection process (2000-2018)
recent_changes: Not accepting new applications in 2024 to clear backlog

name: Clean Water Act Section 401 Certification
description: State certification that federally permitted activities will comply with water quality standards. States can deny certification to block projects.
key_delay_factors: Scope of review (activity as a whole vs point discharge); state opposition to fossil fuel projects; pre-filing requirements
quantitative_impact: NY denied Constitution Pipeline (2016), Millennium Valley Lateral; WA denied coal export terminal (2017); OR denied Jordan Cove LNG
affected_project_types: Pipelines, LNG terminals, power plants, hydropower, dredge/fill activities
recent_changes: Trump 2020 rule limiting scope reinstated by SCOTUS (Apr 2022); Biden 2023 rule expanded scope; Trump 2026 proposed rule to limit scope again
reform_status: EPA proposed rule January 2026 to narrow scope and streamline timelines

name: Clean Water Act Section 404 Wetlands Permit
description: Army Corps permit for discharge of dredged or fill material into waters of the US including wetlands.
key_delay_factors: Alternatives analysis (LEDPA); mitigation requirements; Section 401 certification needed; NEPA compliance; ESA consultation
quantitative_impact: Individual permits: 264 days average (FY2018); Nationwide Permits: 45 days average; Emergency permits: expedited
affected_project_types: Pipelines, transmission lines, infrastructure, mining, development
recent_changes: Sackett v EPA (2023) narrowed WOTUS jurisdiction; Trump emergency procedures using national energy emergency declaration
reform_status: Nationwide Permit 12 for oil/gas pipelines requires individual 404 permits

name: NEPA Environmental Impact Statement
description: Full environmental review required for major federal actions significantly affecting environment.
key_delay_factors: Multi-agency coordination; public comment periods; alternatives analysis; litigation; staff capacity
quantitative_impact: Average EIS takes 4.5 years; 25% take 6+ years; energy projects average 4.5 years; transmission 6.5 years
affected_project_types: Major pipelines, LNG terminals, transmission lines, power plants on federal land
recent_changes: Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023 imposed 2-year deadline; CEQ 2024 reforms; Trump emergency procedures (14 days for EA)
reform_status: Ongoing reform efforts; categorical exclusions expanded for certain clean energy projects

name: Endangered Species Act Section 7 Consultation
description: Consultation with FWS/NMFS to ensure federal actions do not jeopardize listed species or critical habitat.
key_delay_factors: Biological assessment preparation; formal consultation 90-day clock; extensions; BiOp litigation; multiple species
quantitative_impact: 35,000+ project review requests since Nov 2022; workload rising with IRA/IIJA projects
affected_project_types: All federally permitted energy projects in areas with listed species
recent_changes: Trump emergency procedures allow expedited informal consultation under national energy emergency
reform_status: 2024 rule changes; IPaC tool reduces staff time for 10% of projects

name: National Historic Preservation Act Section 106
description: Review of federal undertakings for effects on historic properties. Consultation with SHPO/THPO and tribes required.
key_delay_factors: SHPO/THPO consultation timelines; tribal consultation; MOA negotiations; no statutory deadline
quantitative_impact: Can add 6-12 months to project timeline; particularly impacts linear infrastructure crossing multiple states
affected_project_types: Pipelines, transmission lines, energy projects on federal land, federally funded projects
recent_changes: Trump emergency procedures: 7-day comment period under national energy emergency
reform_status: NEPA substitution process under consideration for major EIS projects

name: Interstate Transmission Line Siting
description: State-by-state approval for transmission line siting. No federal preemption except limited FERC backstop authority.
key_delay_factors: Multiple state approvals needed; local zoning; landowner opposition; lack of coordination; different standards per state
quantitative_impact: Average 4-11 years for permits; construction adds 2-4 years; some projects 10-12 years total
affected_project_types: Interstate and interregional high-voltage transmission lines
recent_changes: IIJA 2021 clarified FERC backstop authority; DOE CITAP program aims for 2-year federal timeline
reform_status: FERC backstop authority not yet used; 3 potential NIETCs identified Dec 2024

name: Local Solar Zoning and Permitting
description: Local zoning approval for solar farms. Highly variable by jurisdiction. Many local bans or restrictions.
key_delay_factors: Local ordinance restrictions; community opposition; setback requirements; agricultural land restrictions; visual impact concerns
quantitative_impact: 760 projects rejected since 2013; 117 rejected in 2024 alone (78 solar, 39 wind); 73% increase in local restrictions 2022-2023; ~1/3 of projects cancelled; $2M average sunk cost per cancelled solar project
recent_changes: Michigan shifted siting to PSC for projects >50 MW (Nov 2024); Ohio affirmed local rejection rights (2021)
reform_status: Some states preempting local authority; others affirming local control

name: Local Wind Turbine Zoning and Permitting
description: Local zoning approval for wind farms. Significant setback and noise restrictions in many jurisdictions.
key_delay_factors: Setback requirements (some 6,600 ft+); noise concerns; visual impact; community opposition; wildlife concerns
quantitative_impact: Average 14-month delay from community opposition; $7.5M average sunk cost per cancelled wind project; 39 wind projects rejected in 2024
recent_changes: Michigan shifted siting to PSC for projects >100 MW (Nov 2024); various states adding restrictions
reform_status: Mixed trends: some states centralizing, others adding local restrictions

name: Clean Air Act Title V Operating Permit
description: Operating permit for major sources of air pollution.
key_delay_factors: Complex emission calculations; EPA oversight; public notice requirements; permit conditions negotiations
quantitative_impact: Required for power plants, refineries, large industrial facilities
affected_project_types: Gas-fired power plants, coal plants, refineries, large industrial facilities
recent_changes: GHG permitting requirements; Good Neighbor NOx limits affecting some states
reform_status: Standard permitting timelines; varies by state

name: Clean Air Act PSD/NSR Preconstruction Permit
description: Preconstruction permit for new or modified major sources in attainment areas (PSD) or nonattainment areas (NSR).
key_delay_factors: BACT/LAER determination; air quality modeling; public comment; EPA Region review
quantitative_impact: Required before construction of major sources; can affect project timeline by 6-18 months
affected_project_types: New power plants, major plant modifications, large industrial facilities
recent_changes: GHG BACT requirements; EPA 111 rule implications

name: Coastal Zone Management Act Consistency
description: State certification that federally licensed activities are consistent with state coastal management programs.
key_delay_factors: State coastal program requirements vary; can be used to delay/block projects; similar to Section 401
quantitative_impact: Required for LNG terminals, offshore wind, coastal pipelines
affected_project_types: LNG terminals, offshore wind, coastal infrastructure, pipelines crossing coastal zones
